No spam - genuine quotes from vetted UK engine specialists only. 8,000+ Engine Codes 40+ Car Brands 100% Free · No Obligation Make Select Make Series Model Select a model Year Select Model First Engine Code Get Free Engine Quotes At a glance · what your overheating means Match the symptom to the likely cause Temperature gauge rising on hills/load Thermostat or water pump issue Critical £80-£700 Gauge in red + no steam Thermostat failed closed Critical £80-£300 Gauge in red + steam Major coolant leak or head gasket Critical £150-£2,000+ Overheating + white smoke Head gasket failure Critical £550-£2,000+ Overheating + engine won't start Engine seized Critical £2,500-£10,000+ What this usually means in UK cars Overheating is the engine's heart attack Engine overheating is the single most destructive thing that can happen to your engine. When your engine overheats, metal components expand beyond their design limits. Cylinder heads warp. Head gaskets fail. Pistons seize in cylinders. Blocks crack. In our 24,650 quote dataset, we identified five primary causes of overheating: Coolant loss - 40% of cases External leak or head gasket. Repair: £150-£2,000+. Thermostat failure - 25% of cases Stuck closed, no coolant circulation. Repair: £80-£300. Water pump failure - 20% of cases Pump impeller broken or leaking. Repair: £150-£700. Radiator blockage - 10% of cases Blocked or damaged radiator. Repair: £300-£800. Air in system - 5% of cases Low coolant or bleeding issue. Repair: £50-£150. The critical rule: If your temperature gauge enters the red zone, you have seconds to minutes to stop the engine. Every second of overheating causes more damage. The overheating escalation - cost progression From £80 to £10,000 in minutes Stage What Happens Cost 1. Coolant loss System pressure drops, localised overheating £50-£700 2. Thermostat stuck Coolant stops circulating, overheating begins £80-£300 3. Brief overheating Head gasket fails - coolant enters oil/chambers £550-£2,000 4. Prolonged overheating Cylinder head warps - cannot be skimmed £1,000-£3,000 5. Critical overheating Pistons seize, block cracks £2,500-£10,000+ 6. Complete seizure Engine stops - replacement required £2,500-£10,000+ The £5,000+ mistake: Ignoring an overheating warning light for "just a few more miles" is the most expensive decision you can make. The cost escalates from £80 to £10,000 in minutes. Common affected vehicles & engines Overheating issues by make and model Vehicle Common Engine Code Typical Overheating Issue Cost Range BMW 3-Series (E90) N47 2.0d Water pump (electric) failure £400-£700 BMW 5-Series (F10) N57 3.0d Thermostat housing leak £300-£500 VW Golf / Audi A3 EA189 2.0 TDI EGR cooler failure £400-£800 VW Golf / Audi A3 EA888 2.0 TSI Water pump failure £300-£600 Ford Focus / Mondeo 1.6/2.0 TDCi Radiator leak £300-£600 Ford Fiesta 1.0 EcoBoost Head gasket (known issue) £600-£1,500 Vauxhall Astra 1.6/2.0 CDTi Water pump £300-£500 Mercedes C-Class OM651 2.1d Thermostat housing £200-£500 Audi A4 / A6 EA288 2.0 TDI EGR cooler failure £400-£800 Land Rover Discovery SDV6 3.0 EGR cooler (known issue) £500-£1,200 Mini Cooper N14/N18 1.6 Water pump/thermostat housing £300-£600 Jaguar XF / XJ 2.2/3.0d Thermostat housing £400-£700 Renault Mégane 1.5/2.0 dCi Thermostat failure £200-£400 What people think vs reality The expensive mistake is thinking you can make it home “The gauge is in the red, but I'm nearly there - I'll keep going.” The 30 seconds you save could cost you £10,000. Stop immediately. “I'll open the bonnet and add coolant while it's hot.” Never open the coolant reservoir when hot. Pressurised coolant will spray out and cause severe burns. “The fan will save it - I'll just rev it.” Revving a hot engine increases temperature. Stop the engine immediately. “Overheating is normal on a hot day.” No. Your car's cooling system is designed for any UK weather. Overheating means something is broken. “I'll just use water - it's fine.” Water isn't a substitute for coolant. It boils at a lower temperature and lacks corrosion inhibitors. “The engine will be fine after it cools down.” The damage is already done. Overheating causes warping and gasket failure even if it seems fine afterwards. Turn off the key immediately Wait 30+ minutes - Do not open the bonnet. Coolant is pressurised and can cause severe burns (steam can reach 100°C+) Do not add coolant - Wait for the engine to cool completely Call for recovery - Do not drive. Arrange recovery to a garage Why this is critical: Opening the coolant reservoir while hot causes pressurised coolant to explode outwards Coolant burns are extremely serious - the fluid is sticky and continues to burn skin Steam can cause severe facial and hand burns If you can't pull over safely: Put the car in neutral Turn on the heater (full heat) to draw heat from the engine This gives you a few extra seconds to find a safe place to stop Never: Open the coolant reservoir when hot Add cold water to a hot engine (thermal shock) Keep driving "just to get home" Rev the engine to "cool it down" Book Emergency Recovery + Diagnostic What happens if you ignore it - detailed progression Every second of overheating causes more damage Time What Happens Temperature Cost Seconds Temperature enters red zone. Coolant boils. System pressure exceeds cap limit. 120°C+ £0 (stop now) 30 seconds Localised hot spots form. Cylinder head begins to warp. Head gasket starts to fail. 130°C+ £550-£2,000 1 minute Head gasket fails completely. Coolant enters combustion chambers and oil. 140°C+ £550-£2,000 2-3 minutes Cylinder head warps significantly. Pistons expand in cylinders. 150°C+ £1,000-£3,000 5 minutes Pistons seize in cylinders. Engine stops. Block may crack. 160°C+ £2,500-£10,000+ The real-world rule: If your temperature gauge is in the red for more than 30 seconds, you've likely caused permanent damage. What to do next Stop, cool, inspect, diagnose Step 1: Stop driving (immediately) Pull over safely · Turn off engine · Wait 30+ minutes Step 2: Check coolant level (when cold) Wait at least 30 minutes · Open the coolant reservoir slowly (cover with a cloth) · Check level - is it below minimum? Step 3: Check for visible leaks Look for puddles under the car · Check hoses and radiator for damage · Look for dried coolant (white residue) Step 4: Check oil (dipstick/oil filler cap) Look for creamy/milky substance (mayonnaise) - this confirms coolant in oil = head gasket failure Step 5: Professional diagnostic (£50-£150) A technician will perform a cooling system pressure test, check for exhaust gases in coolant, inspect thermostat and water pump, and check radiator for blockage. Coolant loss - 40% of cases

blocks.answer: £80-£10,000+ depending on the cause and damage. Thermostat: £80-£300. Head gasket: £550-£2,000+. Engine replacement: £2,500-£10,000+.

blocks.question: Can an engine survive overheating?
blocks.answer: Yes - if you stop immediately. If you continue driving, the engine will be destroyed.

blocks.question: Why is overheating so damaging?
blocks.answer: Metal expands when hot. Cylinder heads warp, pistons seize, gaskets fail. Once the engine overheats, the damage is permanent.

blocks.question: What should I do if my car overheats on the motorway?
blocks.answer: Pull over safely onto the hard shoulder. Turn off the engine immediately. Call for recovery. Do not attempt to drive to the next exit.
